blocks: 1. In the top menu click “Work Orders”, then open a work order whose status is Estimate, Approved, In Progress, or Review (click its row in the list). Open its “Lines” tab. Each work order line has its own Parts section beneath it: the “Add Part” button sits in that section, and every part already on the line has an “edit” control at the right-hand end of its row — that control stays invisible until you move the mouse over the row.

2. Your user’s role can edit work order lines. To check it: open “Settings”, click “Roles & Permissions” in the sidebar, click the pencil on the role your user is on, then find the “Work order lines” section and make sure its “Create & Edit” toggle is on.

3. Your role’s work order view mode is set to “Full View”. To check or change it: open “Settings”, click “Roles & Permissions” in the sidebar, click the pencil on the role your user is on, then in the “Work orders” section set “View mode” to “Full View”.

4. The part details modal (titled “New Part Request” when you are adding a part and “Edit Part Request” when you are editing one) is open — on an open Full View inline row you clicked “More options” — and you have typed data into it.

blocks: 1. On the Full View inline add row, type some values, then click “More Options” to open the part details modal.
2. Change a value inside the modal, then cancel the modal with Cancel, the X, or Escape.
custom_steps.text:
1. On the Full View inline add row, type some values, then click “More Options” to open the part details modal.
2. Change a value inside the modal, then cancel the modal with Cancel, the X, or Escape.

blocks: 1. Cancelling the part details modal - via Cancel, the X, or Escape - shows no confirmation and discards nothing.
2. The modal closes and you are returned to the inline row, which still holds the values it had when “More Options” was opened.
3. Any values you changed inside the modal are not carried back to the inline row.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9315 and story SV-9319 (Story 4, Inline Add Part - Full View) and the Inline Add and Edit Parts on Work Order Lines specification (Confluence page 782761986), section S4-R12, read on 7 September 2026.

Note: the spec update of 2026-09-04 reversed the earlier (2026-08-24) behaviour where cancelling the modal asked for confirmation and discarded both the modal and the inline row; cancel now discards nothing and returns to the inline row. This case follows the current spec.

blocks: 1. For a catalog part, the populated description accepts your edit and can be overwritten.
